samples.claim: DeferredEncoding has uint64 buffer_location=1 and buffer_length=2, locating encoded metadata elsewhere. Its rationale is deduplicating identical encodings: global buffers can share across columns, column metadata buffers across pages, or an unusual page-local location can defer loading a large encoding until the page is needed. Reference bounds/cycles are not validated by this message.
samples.evidence:

118 |  * part of the file.  This is most commonly used to allow encodings to be shared
119 |  * across different columns.  For example, when writing a file with thousands of
120 |  * columns, where many pages have the exact same encoding, it can be useful
121 |  * to cut down on the size of the metadata by using a deferred encoding.
122 |  */
123 | message DeferredEncoding {
124 |    /* Location of the buffer containing the encoding.
125 |     *
126 |     * * If sharing encodings across columns then this will be in a global buffer
127 |     * * If sharing encodings across pages within a column this could be in a
128 |     *   column metadata buffer.
129 |     * * This could also be a page buffer if the encoding is not shared, needs
130 |     *   to be written before the file ends, and the encoding is too large to load
131 |     *   unless we first determine the page needs to be read.  This combination
132 |     *   seems unusual.
133 |     */

135 |    uint64 buffer_length = 2;

samples.claim: The MemWAL section introduces ShardStatus ACTIVE=0 and SEALED=1. Drop-table two-phase commit seals a shard to refuse claims reversibly, then deletes on commit or returns ACTIVE on rollback. ShardManifest documents exactly one active writer per shard; shard_id UUID=11 is v4, version uint64=1 matches manifest filename, shard_spec_id uint32=10 is immutable at creation with zero for manual/unmanaged shards, and shard_field_entries repeated=14 stores raw Arrow scalar bytes keyed by field ID and interpreted by ShardingSpec.result_type. The comment explicitly gives little-endian int32 and raw UTF-8 examples.

492 |  */

496 |  * commits (the shard dir is deleted) or rolls back (status -> ACTIVE).
497 |  */

samples.claim: Pending retains polling ownership and suppresses explicit peer wake. In every ordinary result path upstream is restored into state. A ready result takes the waiting waker, releases the mutex and wakes it, then returns the original Poll. A pending poll relies on upstream waking the owning task; if that handle is later dropped, its Drop hands ownership to the survivor. Stream cancellation behavior depends on dropping the handle as well as dropping a temporary next() future.
samples.manual_notes: Pending/restore/wake behavior matches; Drop ownership transfer checked at82-125. Add direct supporting citation.
